claims.text: The initial material is zirconium-alloy fuel cladding with an elemental Cr coating.
A thin, continuous, dense CrN layer should be deposited on top of the elemental Cr coating.
The CrN overlayer will improve the durability and stability of the Cr coating.
The CrN overlayer will reduce premature coating failure caused by elevated-temperature Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
The CrN layer will enhance corrosion and oxidation protection under both normal-water and accident-steam conditions.
The applicable normal subcritical-water conditions are temperatures below 350°C and pressures below 10 MPa.
The applicable accident-relevant steam conditions are temperatures below 1200°C and pressures below 1 MPa.
The proposed protection applies for exposure times up to 1000 hours.
The CrN layer acts as a barrier against further oxidation.
The CrN layer acts as a barrier against corrosion.
The CrN layer reduces elemental transport across the interface.
The CrN layer inhibits the formation of Cr-Zr intermetallic compounds.
The relevant Cr-Zr intermetallic compounds are brittle and unstable.
Inhibiting Cr-Zr intermetallic formation preserves the integrity of the Cr coating.
Preserving coating integrity maintains the coating's protective properties in both service regimes.
Relative to an elemental Cr coating without CrN, the modified coating will show reduced Cr-Zr interdiffusion-related failure.
Relative to the unmodified Cr coating, the modified coating will provide better corrosion and oxidation protection.

contradictions.description: The conditions include normal-water operation below 350°C, whereas the boundary is stated as 350°C–1200°C, which excludes most of that stated normal-water regime.
The boundary gives pressure as '10 MPa - 1 MPa,' a descending and ambiguous range, while the conditions assign separate upper bounds of below 10 MPa for water and below 1 MPa for steam.
